No Java or Maven installed. I'll still create the project files. Let me set up a standard Maven project with SLF4J facade.

Project structure:
```
/work
  pom.xml
  src/main/java/com/example/app/App.java
  src/main/resources/logback.xml
  src/test/java/com/example/app/AppTest.java
```

Maybe add .gitignore. Let me keep it focused. I'll create the pom with slf4j-api and logback-classic, plus JUnit for tests.

Let me think about naming. Since no repo name, I'll use `com.example:logging-demo`. Actually the project "needs a standard logging facade" — SLF4J is the standard facade.

Let me create the files. This is a multi-file task; a todo list could help but it's fairly straightforward. 4+ files though. Let me just do it efficiently.

I'll use a recent stable version: slf4j 2.0.13, logback 1.5.6, junit jupiter 5.10.2, maven-compiler 3.13.0 release 17.

Let me create files.

input.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>logging-demo</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>logging-demo</name>
    <description>Application using SLF4J as a logging facade</description>

    <properties>
        <maven.compiler.release>17</maven.compiler.release>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>

        <slf4j.version>2.0.13</slf4j.version>
        <logback.version>1.5.6</logback.version>
        <junit.version>5.10.2</junit.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <!-- Logging facade: application code compiles/binds only to this. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
            <artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>
            <version>${slf4j.version}</version>
        </dependency>

        <!-- Runtime implementation. Swap this dependency to change the backend
             without touching application code. Scope "runtime" keeps it out of
             the compile classpath. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>ch.qos.logback</groupId>
            <artifactId>logback-classic</artifactId>
            <version>${logback.version}</version>
            <scope>runtime</scope>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.13.0</version>
            </plugin>

            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.2.5</version>
            </plugin>

            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-shade-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.5.3</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <phase>package</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>shade</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <transformers>
                                <transformer
                                        implementation="org.apache.maven.plugins.shade.resource.ManifestResourceTransformer">
                                    <mainClass>com.example.app.App</mainClass>
                                </transformer>
                            </transformers>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

part.text: I'll set up a Maven project using SLF4J (the standard logging facade) with Logback as the runtime implementation.
Now create the App.java using SLF4J, logback.xml, test, .gitignore.

Now logback.xml config in src/main/resources. Important: if logback-classic is runtime scope, the config is still on classpath. Also note that logback.xml is arguably backend-specific config, but that's fine at resources. To keep application truly decoupled, config file is expected. Let me add it.

Also a test. And .gitignore.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<configuration>

    <appender name="CONSOLE" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">
        <encoder>
            <pattern>%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS} %-5level [%thread] %logger{36} - %msg%n</pattern>
        </encoder>
    </appender>

    <root level="INFO">
        <appender-ref ref="CONSOLE"/>
    </root>

</configuration>

Let me quickly verify files.

Created a Maven project using **SLF4J** as the facade:

- `pom.xml` — `slf4j-api` is the only logging dep on the compile classpath; Logback is `runtime` scope so it can be swapped without code changes. Shade plugin builds a runnable fat jar.
- `src/main/java/com/example/app/App.java` and `Greeter.java` — log via `LoggerFactory`/`Logger`, no backend imports.
- `src/main/resources/logback.xml` — backend config (console appender).
- `src/test/java/com/example/app/GreeterTest.java` — JUnit 5 tests.

Note: Java/Maven aren't installed in this environment, so I couldn't run `mvn verify`. To build: `mvn clean package`, then `java -jar target/logging-demo-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar`.

To switch backends later (e.g. Log4j2), replace the `logback-classic` dependency and config — application code stays untouched.
